utterances.text: In several places in the agenda I can -- we can see that the lawful conduct of police is emphasised.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: What about the attitude of state organs with respect to the crimes committed and the perpetrators of those crimes?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the same can be said about that. We can add to that that it was assisted upon the legality of police action and on taking measures against anybody who committed any kind of an offence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: What can be said about the attitude of state organs towards Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. civilians?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is obvious that it was reiterated that the civilians needed to be protected and provided assistance.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: What can be seen from the agenda as to the attitude towards terrorists?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What we can see is that the terrorists were the only ones against whom police needed to take firm action in order to ensure law and order in Kosovo and Metohija.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: What about the attitude of state organs regarding the departure or non-departure of Albanians across the state border?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Regarding those issues, in the agenda we can see that there was a concern regarding that and that various steps were taken or various measures were taken regarding the columns and entire villages which were moving towards Macedonia and Albania in terms of humanitarian assistance provided, registering these people, registering their place of residence and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: What can be seen regarding the return of Albanian and not Albanian refugees to their places of residence and other safe locations?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Out of several entries we can see that there were attempts to return civilians, various methods concerning how to ensure that return, and other concrete steps that were taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: What about the information available to state organs concerning the urging, attempts urging -- attempts to urge Albanian residents to move out?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we saw several leaflets to that effect.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: What about the issue of sanitisation? What was the attitude of state organs concerning the clearing up of the terrain and sanitisation?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is obvious that it was implied that under that term "sanitisation" we meant all the steps that needed to be taken in order to clear up the terrain; to remove corpses, to remove carcasses, to ensure communication, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: The agenda in its totality, does it clearly reflect what was the intention of our state organs? Did they want the people to move out or to remain?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They absolutely were not in favour of moving out. The moving out was something that caused concern of state organs. They did everything they could to prevent it. The only way they could have prevented it was to use force, and in our assessment the use of force was impermissible.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Since Mr. Nice put questions to you regarding the agenda, please tell us, the totality of the agenda, does it indicate that Mr. Nice took out some sentences out of context and distorted them?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: No. That's totally out of order.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General. We're now going to turn to the footage shown by Mr. Nice about the crime involving the execution of six persons. Did you have occasion to see the entire footage?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw only what was shown during my testimony.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the audiovisual booth play just a few excerpts that I would like witness to comment upon. Professor Rakic has marked everything and it should be in the booth.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell us, what date can we see here, General? General, can you see the date?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I still don't have it on my screen.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the 25th of June, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: By showing this footage, were we supposed to infer, to conclude that the priest was blessing people who were about to commit a crime or something else?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was not my impression that the criminals were being blessed. If I remember correctly, what happened actually took place after that or subsequently.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic. What did that scene indicate to you? You have said what it did not. I'm asking what did it indicate to you?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This scene --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I've asked the witness the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course if we put aside the knowledge that I acquired about what happened afterwards, this scene depicts an Orthodox custom that is performed with respect to persons in uniform. So I, of course, now exclude what I knew about what happened subsequently. There was no way for me to know what would happen after this.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Robinson, it was my intention to emphasise that by presenting it in this way, Mr. Nice in fact insulted the Serbian Orthodox Church because this has nothing to do with what happened afterwards. Would you please play the following excerpt.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I'm quite used to the accused's inappropriate and unjustified remarks, but he seems to be exceeding himself today. Can I invite the Chamber to restrain him from descending any further into personal observations, which are unmerited and inappropriate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Milosevic; refrain from such remarks.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would the audio booth play the following excerpt, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I hope you remember the date. It was the 25th or the 26th. Can you see the date here?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The 26th of June, 1995.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Please continue. Please play on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: The following excerpt is dated when?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 27th of June, 1995.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please play on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: There's no date here. We can see the date. Can you tell us the date?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 30th of June, 1995.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please play on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: What date can we see now?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 1st of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please play on.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The 3rd of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, since you didn't see the entire footage, were you able to see that after the 3rd of July in this entire two-hour footage there is not another single date indicated?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was not able to see that if you are referring to the footage that was shown previously. Today I saw only one excerpt without a date.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: What I'm trying to say is that in the entire tape following the 3rd of July, 1995, there is no single other date indicated.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would you please play the second tape, or the second excerpt you received.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I think we have already seen this here, but the other tape. You saw this cut immediately after one scene depicting a conversation taking place in a company where there are some females as well. There is a cut and we move to this scene taking place in a truck.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You as a person who is experienced in police investigation, would you say that this was a compilation, that this was added on later?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: That is an astonishing leading question. Just because this is being clearly played out for a different audience, let me make it quite plain: This tape was identified by the limited extracts played in order that the witness could have the opportunity to help, as he had said he was inclined to do, with identification of people shown as murderers. In the light, he hasn't come back with any further information and there have been developments we know about. The detailed history of this film will be available in the application that will be made that this video should be produced as an exhibit in due course, and it is quite inappropriate for the accused, after I don't know how many warnings this morning, to ask a question in the form he did, plainly aimed at an objective other than getting helpful evidence before this Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, I am to tell you if you continue in that vein, I will disallow any further playing of this tape. You can ask questions that are not leading. You did so about four or five, ten minutes ago. You asked several questions in relation to the diary, a series of about six questions, and they were put perfectly properly. If you have another purpose to serve by asking leading questions, that will not be facilitated by this Chamber.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Robinson, I hope --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I don't want to hear anything. Just continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please may we see the second tape, 14 minutes, 10 seconds, roughly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Is there a technical problem? We are awaiting the second tape. I understand that the rewinding process is taking place.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, were you able to see the vehicle, the black vehicle?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I saw it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Did you see the sign on it?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And what were the markings or sign on the vehicle?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Obviously it was a vehicle of the army belonging -- of Srpska Krajina. The three letters I can recognise and know they belong to the number plates which belong to the army of the Republic of Srpska Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. And did you see the picture on the door of the vehicle and what --

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And what did it say there?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It said "Detachment," "Odred," and I saw a Skorpion sign, but I don't know what it said underneath that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Did you see that it said "Odred Boca," "Detachment Boca"?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw the "Detachment" part and the picture of the Skorpion, but I wasn't able to see the "Boca" part.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, it's Mr. Nice's tape and we can see that on the tape, but tell us, General, please, whether any kind of markings of that type or vehicle or name Detachment, whether it could ever have been part of a police unit of any kind belonging to Serbia?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I say with full responsibility no, and I stand by what I said earlier on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my answer, while you're looking for your next question, I said quite clearly that to the best of my knowledge gained in August and September 1995 was that that unit belonged to the army of the Republic of Srpska Krajina. I didn't, of course, see on the previous footage the licence plate and --

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: It says "Odred," "Detachment," and underneath it says "Boca."

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I can see that now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Right. Well, we've seen that now. Now let's just hear what it says at 1:47. The time is 1:47. What can we hear there? [Videotape played].

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Now, did you clearly hear, in Serbian it was, and the dialect is not one spoken in Serbia proper but I'm interested in the words, did you hear them say, "Let somebody say that those are the people arrested -- are taken prisoner there and there"?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I heard that, but I didn't hear any geographic location mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: But you heard somebody say, "Those are the ones taken prisoner," et cetera?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And nowhere on the tape do we hear who they are or where they were taken prisoner. You can just hear a voice saying, "Those are the ones captured there," and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Milosevic, there's a part of that question which was leading.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have to observe the accused seems now absolutely determined to take no notice of the warnings and instructions that the Court is giving him, and I invite the Court to have in its mind, maybe at the back of its mind, as I've said before, that if he really will not obey with the orders of the Court, there is an assigned counsel who can take over from him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, it is clear that you are not attending to the warnings being given by the Trial Chamber. You continue to ask leading questions. I'm going to ask Ms. Higgins to be on standby to conclude this re-examination. I don't want to hear from Ms. Higgins now, but she will be on standby if you continue in that way.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, were you able to conclude from what Mr. Nice said where this crime took place, the one that was filmed, the killing of those six young men?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I remember correctly, judging by the indictment, the crime was committed in the environs of Trnovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Fine. Now may we place on the overhead projector a map. It is a Microsoft map. The author is Route eXpress European where we can see the road running between Srebrenica and Trnovo. And it says that the scale is 159.4 kilometres, or, rather, the distance. Take a look at that, please, the distance 159.4 kilometres. Srebrenica is at the beginning of the green line. Can you see where it says Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And can you see down at the bottom there, at the end of the road, it says Trnovo?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So that road had to be a shorter road because you couldn't go through Sarajevo, across Sarajevo, but below Sarajevo, but the distance is 150-odd kilometres. Can that be challenged at all? Is that in dispute at all?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember it, I think the distance would be right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, it says so. It says on the computer map. Srebrenica, Trnovo, depart Srebrenica, end Trnovo, and the distance given is 159.4 kilometres. I don't think I need place that on the overhead projector. Everybody can find it to look up on the Microsoft programme the Route eXpress. General -- well, we don't need the map any more. Thank you. On the basis of what you were able to see, General, and what was shown on the footage, is that undoubtedly a crime?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Is what a crime?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The execution, the shooting. Is that undoubtedly a crime?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: That's not a question for this witness.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Now, General, on the footage did you see something that indicates the time at which the crime was perpetrated?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. I don't think I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: On the footage, were you able to see or conclude something that would indicate who the victims were, where they came from, except for the fact that we hear somebody say that somebody should say who they are and where they were from?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I wasn't able to hear anything like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And is there anything on the footage which would indicate where those young men were executed, what place, what location?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not able to recognise anything from the footage we saw.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And on the footage were you able to see anything that -- to show that the perpetrators of the crime, as Mr. Nice claims, were the members of the MUP of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nothing on the footage showed me that that thesis would be right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, Mr. Nice had a witness here. His name was Dejan Anastacijevic, and he made a presentation. He showed us an article from the newspaper Vreme of the 25th of December, 2003.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, just a minute, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Continue, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: As we were saying, in the magazine Vreme, Dejan Anastacijevic, and the issue was 677, that particular issue, he said that the commander of the Skorpions, Slobodan Medic Boca, at the trial that was held in Serbia against his co-fighters because of the crimes committed in 1999 in Podujevo -- let me just take a moment here to find this. And this is how he described - and I'm quoting from Vreme now - the formation. It was an article on The Sting of a Skorpion. That was the title. "Slobodan Medic Boca, commander of the Skorpions, said at the trial about the history of his unit, although two statements on that same subject tend to differ, that on the 28th -- on the 28th of March he stated that the Skorpion unit was established already in 1991 within the composition of the army of Yugoslavia," and in brackets it says "sic" here, "sic." Now, did the army of Yugoslavia exist in 1991 or was it the Yugoslav People's Army at the time?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1991 what was in existence was the Yugoslav People's Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Then further down the article in Vreme, it says the following: "Several months later, on the 5th of December, the commander Boca gave the following answer to the same question. The Skorpion unit was established in May 1992, he said, as security for the oil industry of Krajina, and in that capacity it remained there from 1992 until 1996." Now, this period of time from 1992 to 1996, does that cover the period which Mr. Nice stipulated here as being the period of time of the execution of these young men?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course it does cover that time, because we were talking of 1995. That was the year.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Right. Now, from the footage were you able to establish when the execution took place?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not from the footing -- footage, no, but I said what the Prosecutor -- what the Prosecutor had said.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You, Mr. Stevanovic, at one point in time, and I made a note of this, when asked by Mr. Nice, you said that -- do you challenge that they were in Srebrenica? Does that mean that you don't challenge that they were in Srebrenica or you don't challenge what the Prosecutor showed us?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember having said that. Maybe I said that I have no reason to doubt that the people on the footage were in Srebrenica. Perhaps that's what I said. But at this point in time, I really can't say, and I can't give you a specific answer to the question because I'm not quite clear about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Fine. Now, do you have a single piece of information saying that they were in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I don't, no. Except what I heard from the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. I'm going to go on quoting that same article of Dejan Anastacijevic, and it says the following: That they were established in May 1992, and that in that capacity, they remained until 1992 -- from 1992 to 1996. Now, the next sentence is: "After that ..." after 1996 that means, "... as I asked my unit to become -- be within the composition of MUP of Serbia the Skorpions entered the reserve force of the special anti-terrorist units of the MUP of Serbia." Now, in the article here by Dejan Anastacijevic and from the trial in Belgrade, can we see that their status, the status of these --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Stop, Mr. Milosevic, and reformulate.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: According to what is written here in this article in Vreme, when it says that they were in that capacity of protecting the oil industry of Krajina from 1992 until 1996, and then it says after that they became part of the reserve force. So what would be the earliest point when they could have become part of the reserve force of the MUP of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the earliest point, and if I remember correctly, that corresponds to those two documents that the Prosecutor showed yesterday, that time could have been after the end of the war in Republika Srpska Krajina and in Republika Srpska. That means after mid-1996, or after the beginning of 1996. That would be the earliest point.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Now, I've read this out to you, and what can your conclusion be? Who did these Skorpions belong to?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I already said very clearly that in 1995, in the autumn of 1995, I knew that that unit belonged either to the army or police of Republika Srpska Krajina. So all my knowledge, including what you quoted just now, indicates what I already said. That unit belonged, and it's obvious by the licence plates, to the army of Srpska Krajina, up to the end of the war, that is up to 1996.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Now, I'm to quote to you a transcript of witness Milan Milanovic who testified for Mr. Nice's side. Mrs. Uertz-Retzlaff conducted the examination. I'm just going to quote very briefly from 27431. That was the page. Q is question: "[In English] Just a very few -- a final question in relation to the Skorpions. You have described the Skorpions --" [interpretation] she's putting questions to Milanovic -- "[In English] being involved and sent to the Bihac region. When they were in this region, to whom were they subordinated then?" Answer: "They were subordinated to the command of the army of the Republic of Serbian Krajina." [Interpretation] Next quotation on transcript page 27432, again Mrs. Uertz-Retzlaff putting the question: "[In English] You also mentioned the Skorpions being present in Trnovo in Bosnia in 1994."

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: When Skorpions were in Trnovo, to whom were they subordinated?" Answer: "To the MUP of the Republika Srpska." [Interpretation] Then further on: "[In English] You described the deployment of Skorpions in Kosovo, and especially the first deployment when you accompanied them a short way. At that time, was there a mobilisation in Serbia under way?" Answer: "Yes. The Skorpions went to Kosovo seven or eight days after the NATO bombing. And on the first day of bombing, in the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, a state of war was proclaimed, which meant that the mobilisation was proclaimed and ongoing." Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. [Interpretation] Question: "[In English] And why did Medic call you instead of just getting mobilised with the JNA -- or the VJ in this case?" Answer: "Medic called me because he didn't want him and his men, the men he knew from Slavonia, to go under the command of the army of Yugoslavia. He wanted to go as part of MUP of Serbia."

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: He was returned from there following General Djordjevic's orders? He demanded that he return?" Answer: "Yes. He was returned, but he went back and stayed until the end of bombing raids." [Interpretation] So what can be concluded on the basis of these allegations in respect of the claim that in 1995 the Skorpions belonged to the MUP of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the basis of the text quoted, it is obvious that what I already stated is correct; that in 1995 the Skorpions did not belong to the MUP of Serbia. It would not be logical for them to belong to the MUP of Serbia if they indubitably belonged to the Republic of Srpska Krajina and they went to the territory of Republika Srpska. It would be quite illogical. Why would they change their affiliation? They could go there according to the decision of their own command and then they could be subordinated to the other command there. I don't see why the MUP of Serbia would have to act as any kind of intermediary.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: On the basis of these quotations that you heard from me just now, what can you conclude? Under whose command were they at the time and who did they belong to?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, that is not taking us any further. We have the evidence before us and we will determine those matters.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, we showed now on the footage the licence plates of the vehicle, what can be seen. Now, what can be seen on this film? Does it correspond to what Milanovic said and what Medic himself said about who they belonged to?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was my understanding that it does correspond to what they said.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. At the time of the crime from the footage that Mr. Nice played, did the members of that unit belong to the MUP of Serbia --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, again, I think this is conclusions and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, we're not being helped by that. We have the evidence before us. These are questions of fact for the Chamber to assess on the basis of the evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, lest there being any lingering misapprehension, all the issues that the accused is raising which are matters of detail on the film, parts of which -- almost all of which was not displayed, of course the Prosecution is aware of them, they will be available to be dealt with evidence in due course. I can outline them now if he really wants me to, but I'm sure he doesn't, but it doesn't really take the issue further at all to have partial answers on partial bits of film which was produced for a different purpose, a purpose that in the event is being secured another way by concessions and actions of the authorities in Serbia, but that's another matter. These questions take us no further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Next question, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Robinson, what can be seen on the film, as far as licence plates are concerned, and in terms of what Milanovic testified here when being questioned by --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, I've stopped you. Ask your next question and avoid the comment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, Medic claims, on the basis of what I quoted to you, that members of the unit asked to become part of the reserve force after 1996. Are you aware of any such case or would it be logical for someone who is already within a unit as to belong to a particular army or police?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course if they're already part of the MUP, it would be illogical for them to ask to become part of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. And does the -- is the reserve force of the MUP joined individually or collectively?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already said that very clearly: There is a chapter of the law on the interior which regulates the admission of persons into the police force. In accordance with these provisions, individuals as military conscripts can be admitted into the police force, not a unit in any situation. Of course, Medic could have submitted any kind of request, including that kind of request too, to admit the entire unit, but in accordance with the law, an entire unit could not be admitted. And obviously this did not happen, because they became part of the reserve force of an already existing unit. It is beyond dispute, since yesterday we saw that they were there, but it is also beyond doubt that they were within a special anti-terrorist unit of the MUP. They were recruited, and they were deployed within an existing unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And what was this existing unit?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The special anti-terrorist unit of the public security sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. We established that. Now, tell us, what does it mean to belong to the reserve force of the MUP?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The reserve force is practically an assignment on the basis of military obligation in accordance with the law on military obligation. Somebody can be assigned either to the reserve force of the army or the reserve force of the police or in the civilian protection or simply does not have a specific assignment. Of course, I'm talking about military conscripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. As far as military conscripts are concerned, is every able-bodied person or, rather, may I correct myself, is every able-bodied man in Serbia in some reserve force, either of the army or the police?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. Most military conscripts are on some reserve force. There are exceptions, when it can be said that somebody is without a specific assignment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: While following these proceedings, did you have the opportunity to follow General Vasiljevic's testimony?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I'm just going to read a very brief excerpt from his testimony. The page is 16003. "[In English] Question: Did the accused himself contribute in any positive way, concrete way, on how the criminal problems or the volunteer problems should be addressed?" Answer: "Except for what I have said already, that drastic cases needed to be addressed, that this Boca had to be handed over to the judicial organs," et cetera. [Interpretation] Before that, before that, since he was mentioned at that meeting, since Vasiljevic says that he had already mentioned the context in which I referred to it, on page 16001 of his testimony, he says that I said: "[In English]... that there was no reason to protect them." [Interpretation] I put it another way. I said that there was no reason to. "[In English] And secondly, he said that such drastic cases as were mentioned have to be urgently sanctioned and dealt with and that the so-called great Serbs acting in these ways and committing crimes were inflicting great damage to everything that Yugoslavia," et cetera, et cetera. [Interpretation] Do you know that that pertained to a meeting held with me and Vasiljevic, who testified here against me? He spoke about the attitude towards the reports received at that time in Kosovo and Metohija.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I don't know about that quotation, and I don't know about that meeting. I can say something important, though. This kind of description of an answer completely fits into the thesis that we saw two or three times in my notebook. There are no private wars, that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that members of that group, some members of that group, in 1999, when they volunteered to join the ranks of the MUP, that they carried out some crime?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't remember the date when they were admitted, but that is obviously on the documents that we saw yesterday. The crime committed by the members of that group is contained in the documents here, and I described it several times. This is a crime committed in Podujevo, and some members of that unit killed 17 or 19 civilians, if I remember correctly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me now, General, were these persons arrested and were criminal proceedings brought against them?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I also said that urgently the entire group was returned from Kosovo after that. The investigating procedure was also urgent. Very quickly the case was solved, a criminal report was filed, and after awhile at least one perpetrator of that crime was arrested.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Is this criminal report contained in our tab 152 that has to do with your evidence here?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is here, but let me just find it, please. Do I need to find it?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Just tell me, what can you infer on the basis of the membership of these persons in MUP forces in 1999 from this criminal report?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it says very clearly that they are members of the reserve force of the special anti-terrorist unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Let's not waste any time over that now.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is quite clear. "Cvjetan Sasa and Demirovic Dejan, together with a few perpetrators unknown, as members of the reserve force of the SAJ." It is clearly stated on the first page of the criminal report.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether these persons before the war started were engaged in any form, even in the reserve force of the MUP of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I'm absolutely unaware of any such fact. Or, rather, I don't know anything about this. I am sure that if they belonged to the Skorpions from Eastern Slavonia, that they were not in the MUP of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Now look at this document that Mr. Nice presented yesterday. That is a letter sent to the head of the public security sector, General Djordjevic. It says, "A report on the engagement of the reserve force for the needs of special anti-terrorist units."

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I be allowed to see the document, please, if you want me to comment on it?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I hope you received it yesterday.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did, but it was taken back.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Unfortunately, I don't have the number. Mr. Nice presented the document yesterday. It was a letter sent to or, rather, sent by the commander of the special anti-terrorist unit to General Djordjevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: No documents have been marked at the moment because of our position on production of documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I handed over mine in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Is it the letter from Colonel Trajkovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have received that document. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, microphone for the accused.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I had the impression that the microphone was switched on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: But anyway, Colonel Trajkovic was the commander of the special anti-terrorist unit; is that right?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: At the beginning here, where it says "Subject" --

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, what does it say? What is the subject?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Report on the engagement of the reserve force for the requirements of the SAJ."

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So it is a report on the engagement of the reserve force for the requirements of the special anti-terrorist unit; is that right?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 2, does it say that the SAJ needed to be reinforced by a certain number of reservists? Is that what it says?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is exactly what it says, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And then in paragraph 3, it says the following or, rather, can you read out what it says, the first sentence. Or I can read it out: "With agreement from the head of the public security sector and the staff of the MUP of Pristina, 128 members of the reserve force were engaged who were placed on the list of the reserve force of the special anti-terrorist unit."

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So is any mention made here about any unit called the Skorpions in this letter? Any mention of the Skorpions there?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The name of the unit is not mentioned. In continuation, all that is mentioned is Medic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Who brought them in the first place?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Now, the special anti-terrorist unit, was it an integral unit?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was an independent autonomous unit within the public security sector, of course integral with all the necessary structure and formation and establishment components.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: On the basis of what it says here, it says: "... engaged 128 members of the reserve force from the list of the reserve force of the special anti-terrorist unit." Now, from what it says there, these reservists, were they engaged individually or as a unit?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is clear that they were engaged individually. Even in this text I can't see any mention of any different description of their engagement.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: How, then, can you explain that in the second document that was compiled in the year 2002 --

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I see the document, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, it was handed over by Mr. Nice yesterday in a pair. Both documents were supplied. And this dates back to the time when the event took place, when individuals were engaged for the reserve force, as you've just established. Now, how do you explain the 2002 document where mention is made of the Skorpion unit?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Is it 2002 or 2001?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 2002. The 11th of March 2002 is the date.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I be allowed to see the document, if possible, please, because I haven't got it in front of me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: The draft translation omits the date of the 11th of March 2002 and picks it up only with the other date further down, which refers to the 17th of July 2001. If you look at the original --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: -- date.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I've found it, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The one we have has the date the 17th of July.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Report to the district court investigations department.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have here a document of the 11th of March, 2002. Perhaps this isn't such a good copy. Perhaps it should be an 8 rather than a 3 for the month.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: This is the same document. It's clear that the original document has the date 11th of March on it and that got omitted in the draft translation, which was done in a great hurry, I know. It's also clear that the date of the 17th of March is, it appears, the date of something else. Whether it's the date of the letter of referral or the date of the order or whatever it is, in the draft translation the word "connection" is used, and so here we have a document of the 11th of March, 2002, as the accused says, apparently responsive to an earlier document of the 17th of July 2001, and pending provision of a final translation, it might be sensible if we hand wrote the addition of the date 11th of March 2002 onto the English version, and indeed the name -- the word "Belgrade."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I heard somebody mention July. So that's why I reacted and said that it said March in my copy. But I don't know the document because I haven't received it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: But my question is this for you, General, regarding this matter: Since previously we went through the letter that the commander of the special anti-terrorist unit sent to General Djordjevic, and it refers to the engagement of the reservists, my question to you is this: As this document is -- it says that "The department for struggling against organised crime acted pursuant to your request for gathering information as part of the investigation"; is that right?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Then it says here: "The accused Cvjetan Sasa and Demirovic Dejan, in the course of March 1999, were members of the Skorpion unit." Now, I would like you to clear up this point, the contradiction here, because in the letter by the commander it says that 128 members of the reserve force, who were brought in by Medic, were included, as you explained, into the anti-terrorist unit, whereas here it says that they were members in 1999 of the Skorpion unit.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my -- in answering yesterday's questions, I focused upon the fact of whether people who were in the reserve force, whether they belonged to that unit from the previous period and whether they were indeed in Kosovo, and I of course agreed when I saw the documents which I hadn't seen beforehand. Now I'm focusing my attention on what you've just highlighted, and certainly an assertion of this kind quite simply is not correct, cannot be correct, and it would not have been in conformity with the law for a number of reasons. We have explained several of them when we spoke about legal procedure and membership in the reserve force. Now, the fact -- a key fact is that a second unit, another unit, had not been established. A new unit, or the new unit, within the frameworks of the ministry can be formed only if there are amendments to the rules and regulations governing administration, and the reserve force is included into the existing peacetime units, into their structure, and that's what was done here. And the third fact is this: Not a single unit within the frameworks of the Ministry of the Interior never ever had an official title of this kind written in inverted commas, that is just not possible. So I cannot say here what the fact is or argument is on the basis of which this text could have been formulated in this way.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Fine. But as far as I was able to understand, the allegations in the letter of Colonel Trajkovic is something which is in line with what you know about the whole matter; is that right?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Now, General, a group of reservists of the special anti-terrorist unit arrived, as it says here. A number of those men committed a crime and they were arrested. We reached that stage; right?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Now, in that way, was the law acted upon, were the actions in conformity with the law, or were there attempts made to cover up the crime?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely not. There were no attempts to cover up the crime. Every criminal report and investigation is a public matter and an arrest is public. Everything that was done was done publicly and in conformity with the law. Including what I have said here a number of times, that the urgent return of this group of people for which it was -- there was suspicions that they had taken part in a crime, they were returned from Kosovo post haste.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: But the investigation further established who committed the crime and that person or those persons were arrested; is that right?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Fine. Now, General --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Robinson, could we receive some information as to when this footage was taken, when the tape was filmed, who taped, who took it, when Mr. -- when it came into Mr. Nice's possession and so on, the tape shown by Mr. Nice. And is there a single fact, and you saw the map where Trnovo is and where Srebrenica is, that could link this up to Srebrenica in any way? Because I really would like to ask the question -- the witness some questions in that regard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nice.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I'm quite happy to provide a certain amount of information, although the detailed information will come available in the form of a witness statement which will probably initially be served confidentially and the course of witness concerned is a protected person, as he would have to be. As to the source of the tape, no, I have no intention of providing any information of that at the moment. As to the identification of the tape by a witness, the identification is by a witness who was present and who took a large part of the video, who handed the machine on to the person who took the last part of the video, and who is able to speak of the continuity of the tape and of the fact that the tape records the killing of people brought from Srebrenica in batches for killing. That's the information I've got, and if the accused wants to know it, that's what it amounts to. As to the location, we've working on the basis that it's at Trnovo, as displayed on the map, and I think that may be right, but in any event, the location of the site can be established by the exhumation process. We're just trying to get the precise grid reference right now. The exhumation process that is part of the process whereby these young men were capable of being identified by name, or some of them. So that's in short order what I'm able to provide in answer to the issues raised by the accused, but this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: When will the witness statement be provided?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, the position is to some degree dependent on whether the video is itself produced as an exhibit at this stage. If it isn't, I shall therefore have to make an application to have it produced, which perhaps is what I forecast having to do, it will come when the general application to add evidence of this type is before you, which is in preparation at the moment. The Court will have in mind no doubt, having seen the documents produced in relation to the presence in this area and at this time of troops or groups recorded in the documents as either MUP or Skorpions or sometimes both, that those documents are also documents for which I might be seeking leave to add material at this stage, and I want the whole thing to be dealt with compendiously. Indeed, the Chamber may recall at an earlier stage when I indicated or intimated that there would be an application to reopen, I also intimated - and I think this is writing but I'm not now quite sure - that the completion of that process would be dependent on security arrangements being made for witnesses or a witness, and that's the position in which we found ourselves until very recently when I was able to deal with this tape. So far as -- let me just look at the accused's questions, because I think there may have been something else I wanted to help you with. The -- as to -- I'm so sorry. As to linkage -- yes. As to linkage to Srebrenica, there will, I think, be available to you material from relations and the bereaved of one or more of those killed tying the person to Srebrenica and identifying the body exhumed, and I understand that indeed the relevant commission that's been dealing with exhumations and that therefore took over this site once it was discovered that there were bodies there, is in a position to confirm that the site is the Trnovo near Sarajevo to which people were brought in in lorries because of the need to kill people -- killing people is a huge exercise. It's not something that -- killing and burying. They were taken away from Srebrenica to distant locations, and here's one of them, and that's what happened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: 150 miles -- 150 kilometres. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Yes. In the back of the lorry, arriving in the condition we can see. And I think the accused omitted to touch on this detail but indeed one of the soldiers, I think kneeling beside one of the young men, mocks him with the fact --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: -- arise whether the video, without more, without any additional evidence, does it establish the proposition that you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: It may not. It may. It's a matter for -- there are, of course -- there have, of course, been reactions and acknowledgements in Serbia, which may -- by government sources, which may be of considerable value.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Nice, have these victims been identified?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I think the position is that two were already identified before the video was displayed at all. As you realise, it was displayed in very short order here and much more extensively in Serbia, but as a result of its being screened in Serbia, I think at least one more was identified by relations seeing him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: One issue that's been identified in the submission by Mr. Milosevic is the link to Srebrenica, and what he's asking for is what's the material so that he can, if appropriate, ask questions of this witness. Now, you --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: The linkage will come in two ways; from a witness who will deal with it directly and then indirectly, if necessary, by indication of the people shown being killed and other evidence connecting them to Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: If you -- if you receive permission to produce that evidence. When you --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Absolutely. Your Honour is quite right. Absolutely. Of course. It's all contingent on that but this is clearly an issue of importance and value and something that simply was never available to us before, so we would anticipate making, if necessary, an application. I had, of course, given thought to the question of whether the whole video was capable of self-production, but there are various matters, one or two of which -- to which the accused has referred that make that less rather than more possible. For example, the number plates issue. Of course it's a matter we've addressed and it's dealt with evidentially and indeed it's explained, the same way as may be evidence about the change of patches as things cross borders, but that will have to be matter of evidence, I suspect, in some stage and in some setting. I think -- let me just have a look at the accused's questions again. That probably is as far as I should and can go in answer to these questions at this stage. But Your Honours, we've had very much in mind the desirability from the Chamber's point of view of having applications either for reopening or for rebuttal dealt with in collections, or preferably in a single application, because it must be more convenient for the Court, for the assigned counsel, and for the accused, and we are working energetically on getting the material together so that you can have a single application very soon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Ms. Higgins.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Your Honour, very briefly. The problem with the video from the start, as was identified by Mr. Kay, was that there was no foundational basis laid. I don't wish to address you in detail on that, but the issues relating to who were the victims, who were the perpetrators, where this was exactly, and when, have only been put forward as assertions by Mr. Nice and there is no evidence before the Trial Chamber to deal with it. Dealing with the request made by Mr. Milosevic, it's my submission that he is entitled to know the foundation and the material that is within the Prosecution's possession and to be given that material immediately, as soon as possible. If there is a witness statement in the hands of the Prosecution, then that should be turned over.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just -- you're saying that if he has a witness statement, it should be turned over to Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: It should be disclosed to Mr. Milosevic and the parties, yes, Your Honour, along with any other foundational material which will, I assume, be relied on in due course by the Prosecution to attempt to exhibit the material.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: And if he -- if he doesn't attempt to exhibit it?

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Well, there's an argument that one is entitled to know the foundations upon which the assertion is made.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: So he has a disclosure obligation.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Under 66 --

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: If I may just consult the Rules. I don't have them just before me. Your Honour, if you have 66(B) in front of you, it relates to material for the preparation of the Defence or intended for use by the Prosecutor as evidence at trial, and the issue of non-disclosure previous to the showing of the video was raised by Mr. Kay. The word being "material" as opposed to evidence having been exhibited.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: So that even if he's not successful in an application to introduce this by way of additional evidence or in rebuttal, your submission is that he has an obligation under 66(B) --

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: -- to disclose it.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Yes. Because it's material to the preparation. It may be material to the preparation of the Defence and allow Mr. Milosevic to actually deal with what is being put forward in a very brief form at the moment. It's very difficult to deal with something when one isn't aware, apart from assertion, as to where it comes from and what it actually is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Nice, anything on 66(B)?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Not particularly, no. I mean, if I could --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for Mr. Nice, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Not particularly. I mean, the suggestion that if the accused makes a request he's entitled to have anything material to the preparation of his Defence means that we have to assess whether this is material to his Defence, but I suspect that probably --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I mean, it is -- that is, Mr. Nice --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: That is evident.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: That can be short-circuited, in any event, because I think we're either at or nearly at the time when the witness statements or draft witness statements can be handed over. However, they might require orders of protection from the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: That's a different matter. That's a different matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: And so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The view which we take is that Ms. Higgins is right in her submission that you have a disclosure obligation under 66(B) in relation to material relating to the tape.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Yes, when he makes a request.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, he has made a request.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: As he has made. I agree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: He has made a request.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: But only today. And indeed, I mean, it is important to have in mind the narrow purpose and manner in which I introduced the material, even if the purpose that I introduced it for has been short-circuited by reactions elsewhere. But, Your Honours, what I can do, and I don't think it will take me any time at all, is check on whether there are any outstanding issues, and I don't believe there are, that inhibit the production of either full or certainly redacted statements at this stage, subject to any questions of protection for which I will seek the Court's assistance if necessary. That can be done. But it can't be done literally now. There is also other material, and I am obliged to one of my colleagues for confirming this in answer to one of the accused's questions. Two -- oh, His Honour Judge Bonomy's question as well, I think. Two of the identifications are by DNA analysis, and that material will have to be available. Whether it's immediately available to us or not I'm not sure. And as I already indicated, certainly one the witness statements is only a draft at the moment, but that is probably a technicality. Otherwise, I don't have any particular problem with the request.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Nice, we take account of the fact that the accused has only made his request for this material today.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: But we would expect you, in fact we would require you to report to the Chamber on the next sitting day, which is Wednesday of next week, on that matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'll try and do better than that, and if there is no impediment, I'll hand the material over today or tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Your Honours, just very briefly. In terms of the identity of the witness statement maker, as I understand it, Mr. Nice would have to apply for protective measures, otherwise Mr. Milosevic is entitled to know the identity of the maker of the statement, surely, in accordance with the Rules.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, I think he indicated that he would.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: On that topic, of course, the position with sensitive witnesses in the course of the Prosecution's case was that there was a shortened period when the full details had to be made available to the accused, and until that time, until that triggered time started, then he was not entitled to those details for certain categories of witnesses. We haven't encountered this particular procedural issue in the course of the Defence case thus far. We may have to look and see whether the same rules would apply, assuming, if it be the case, that I find there are security issues relating to witnesses or potential witnesses that require protection. I'll deal with all that immediately.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Very well, yes. Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Robinson, I would like to draw your attention first of all to what Mr. Nice said a few minutes ago. You can see it in the transcript. I wrote it down properly. He said, verbatim, that the link between what he showed will be established. Please bear that in mind. Is that an appropriate way to act? On all world TV stations and Serb TV stations, it has been said time and again that this is footage from Srebrenica. And Mr. Nice says now that he is yet to establish the link showing that this has to do with Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, whether he establishes the linkage or not is a matter for the Chamber. We have no concern with the public's perception of the matter. Ultimately we will examine all the evidence before us and come to a conclusion as to the worth, the value of the -- of the tape.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Robinson, but he said, he spoke in the future that he has yet to establish this linkage. I assume that if he is asserting something, he has to prove that there is this kind of linkage, and it is only then that he can work on that basis, not for him to play footage here that has nothing to do with Srebrenica whatsoever. And you saw that it is 150 or, rather, 160 kilometres away from Srebrenica, and then he promises that he has yet to establish by way of a witness linkage between that footage and what happened in Srebrenica. And on the footage you do not even have the actual place where it was filmed and the time when it was filmed. I do not understand this kind of handling of evidence at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, those are matters for us. We will determine -- we haven't made any determination as to the production of the tape as an exhibit. We have another three or four minutes, four minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, whatever passage of my observations the accused wrote down, I made it quite clear the material to make the linkage is indeed already with us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, we have another three, four minutes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please. I just wish to have one more thing clarified for me. A few moments ago, Mr. Nice claimed that the prisoners from Srebrenica were driven to Trnovo so that they would be killed there. Can you give me information from Mr. Nice how, within some kind of operation, prisoners were transported to Trnovo? Can he do that through you? Secondly, he claimed that the persons who carried out this execution, which is indubitably a crime, were from Serbia. In the documents and the statement of this witness you saw that it has nothing to do with Serbia, that these are not persons from Serbia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, as I said, those are all matters which the Chamber will have to determine on the basis of all the evidence before it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm sorry to interrupt, but I see the time. It looks, extraordinarily, as though the re-examination of this witness is not going to finish today. If that's the case, I have a small administrative matter I'd like to mention relating to the next witness. It can only take 30 seconds but I'd better do it before the magical hour of 2.43 [sic].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Well, do it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: And it's this -- it's this, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I just need five seconds, five seconds for yet another request. Because you entrusted Mr. Nice with providing certain information on the following working days, since you're talking about technical matters in relation to this highly suspicious tape, as far as I'm concerned. What is said in the footage where obviously there has been some deletion? You saw part of the film where it says it should be read out who they are and where they were taken prisoner, and then part of the sound is deleted. I'm sure that Mr. Nice has the appropriate technical facilities, because you can only hear mumbling like when the voice of a protected witness is scrambled here, in order to hear what is said in that footage. I have the right to hear that and I have the right to know why this was deleted and why it was scrambled.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Nice, the accused says that there is a portion of the tape that was deleted.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: He has a transcript --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for Mr. Nice, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: He has the transcript in English and B/C/S exactly the same that we have and that is, as I understand it, complete in all available particulars. I -- we've arranged -- I certainly remember arranging to have every word transcribed, and he's got everything that we've got.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: He says you have everything, everything was played.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Not everything was played.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Not everything was played, but nothing was deleted --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: No, nothing was deleted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: -- in relation to what was played. Nothing was deleted from the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Nothing was deleted from the transcript, and we have the copy or whatever it is of the video identified by a witness or a potential witness. The video comes in, the soundtrack is described, and as I understand it, it's not -- it's not of a quality on which we can engineer improvements.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: So that's your answer, Mr. Milosevic. What's the administrative matter?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, the next witness is a witness for whom we were expecting to start today. I prepared or had prepared for him two binders of materials. They would have served the purpose of a voir dire had there been one. They will also serve the purpose of cross-examination, and their pre-reading by the Chamber might save time. If the Chamber feels it might be disposed to pre-read the material, then I'm obviously content that the accused should have the material as well, and Ms. Higgins and anybody else within the Chamber. However, the material includes redacted witness statements that have to be redacted for reasons of security, and were the accused to have the advantage ahead of the witness coming in, which will now be next Wednesday - at least I hope it's Wednesday and not Thursday - of the witness coming in on Wednesday, I would ask that it be on terms that he doesn't himself copy the material any further, because redacted materials are always vulnerable to inquiries of kinds that can uncover identifications and I would be very concerned that that might happen. So in two stages; if the Chamber thinks it might be helped by having the materials in advance as a time-saving exercise, I'm happy for the accused to have them, but may he be instructed not further to copy the materials in any way, and we can decide what, if any, further protection needs to be attached to individual bits of those materials next week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic -- Ms. Higgins.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Just very briefly, Your Honour. I was given a copy of the materials earlier on today, and they are a significant bundle which in this instance may be of use indeed to Mr. Milosevic to have been able to pre-read the materials and to keep them, and also for Defence counsel. I don't know whether Mr. Nice also intends to give them for pre-reading to the witness, but it's certainly material that I wouldn't wish to be withdrawn from us, it being very useful to have and a time-saving device as well as fair.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Ms. Higgins. Mr. Milosevic, you may have the material --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Robinson --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You may have the material, but the material is not to be reproduced or copied.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have fully understood this, Mr. Robinson. As you know, I never abused anything, any of the material I received over these three years and even more. But let me go back to my request. This is a misunderstanding. I did not talk about any deletions in the transcript. I talked about the videotape or, rather, the CD, the video footage, that there is a section where the words were scrambled and also part of the soundtrack was deleted. Of course then that is not in the transcript. I'm seeking explanation with regard to these defects in addition to all the other defects of the videotape where it cannot be seen who, when, where, or anything else for that matter. Certainly what was deleted from the soundtrack cannot be in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Nothing to add to what I've already said. We've got what we've got. We've got evidence about it and the accused got what we've got. If I do make material available to the accused before next Wednesday, unless the Court orders me otherwise, I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Nice, is it not for the reasons of some secretive reasons or just protection of somebody or --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Not to my knowledge but I'll check on it. But this: If I do make it available to the accused, unless ordered otherwise, I will also make it available to the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. The material may be handed over to the accused on the terms that you indicated.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Certainly. But I say I'd also make it available to the Chamber in advance of next Wednesday unless the Chamber tells me it doesn't want it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. I think they are here already.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And then your terms do not prohibit his associates to take a look at --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: No, they can look at it, of course, but this is witness statements and other material providing links to Srebrenica and things of that sort.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The Chamber has the material at hand, Mr. Nice. We are past the time for adjournment. We will adjourn until Wednesday of next week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 15th day of June, 2005, at 9.00 a.m.
